signal_evidence.credit_quality_trend: Both delinquency and write-off rates remain below 2019 levels and delinquency rates have been between 1.2% and 1.3% for over 3 years... provision expense of $1.1 billion included a reserve release of $191 million, mostly reflecting further strengthening of portfolio credit performance.
signal_evidence.services_demand: Global MX travel bookings up 22% year-over-year in the quarter... restaurant spending, our largest T&E category, was up 10%... airline is up 10%, and this is the highest number we've seen in the last 6 quarters.
signal_evidence.capex_direction: We are raising our revenue guidance and now expect full year revenue growth of 10%... we plan to reinvest this outperformance in growth initiatives... marketing to be up by around 10% year-over-year in the second half of the year, driven by increased investments in customer acquisition [plus TheFork acquisition and accelerated technology investment].
signal_evidence.pricing_power: Net card fees reached record levels, and once again our fastest-growing line, up 15.4%... 75% of new accounts acquired on fee-paying products in the quarter, the highest level we have seen since we increased our focus on premium products... retention rates were not only through the roof, they were flat year-over-year [after a $200 Platinum fee increase].
signal_evidence.management_tone_shift: We are tracking ahead of the expectations we set at the beginning of the year... U.S. consumer spending was up 11%, the highest level of growth since Q1 2018, excluding periods impacted by the pandemic... we raised our full year revenue growth guidance to 10%.
